item.title: Software Engineer, AI Coding Tasks, Askable
item.description:
Remote, None, Global

We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

How it works Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate. Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks. Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them. Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it. Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round. Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.

item.title: Junior Machine Learning Engineer, HFT Architecture
item.description:
Remote, Worldwide

HFT Architecture builds short-horizon price prediction and the trading system around it. This role works on the pipeline that turns order-book records into validated models, next to more experienced engineers: data preparation, experiments end to end, and the checks that keep the future out of a training set.

Fully remote, from anywhere in the world. Junior.

Base salary: USD 125,000–155,000 a year.

To apply: a link to your résumé, LinkedIn or GitHub, and one sentence on any of our articles. No file, no cover letter.

Apply: https://hftarchitecture.com/careers/junior-machine-learning-engineer?utm_source=pythonorg&utm_medium=jobboard&utm_campaign=careers-2026-10

You write Python every day, with tests; can explain the machine learning basics, including why ordinary cross-validation breaks on time series; and have one project of your own you can show and talk through.
